findings.claim: The attribute is only emitted under `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so the requirement 'all generated code is decorated' is met only for some target frameworks. The guard is a judgement call about what 'all' means. It also relies on the consuming project defining those preprocessor symbols, which holds for SDK-style projects. The README documents the limitation.

findings.claim: The change does not cover every generated type. Types emitted via other paths, such as the nesting partial types from EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces, the `GetFormatterHelper` static class (decorated only in the ResolverTemplate), and any other helper or attribute emission, are not all decorated. The new test only asserts that the attribute appears at least once per file, not on every type. A file containing an undecorated type would still pass.
